subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr is a cautious observer who summoned Calmer and Thorne, and later led the group toward the Moathouse. He is present during the bridge collapse and kills the final frog with his hand.
source_quote: Zephyr says, “Well, since we are all here, let’s go outside and wait for the rest of the crew.”

subject: Calmer
fact: Calmer is a devout, over-eager cleric of St. Cuthbert, insecure about his first adventure. He insists on leading the party onto the drawbridge, which collapses, causing him to fall into the water and be injured. He survives after being patched up by Zinia.
source_quote: Calmer shouts, “I think it’s time that I did what all great clerics of St. Cuthbert do, which is lead.”

subject: Thorne (Duke)
fact: Thorne, who goes by Duke, is a rugged, scarred man in his late 30s with a weathered face and short brown hair. He is pragmatic, focused on utility, and comments on cooking frog legs. He sets up camp beyond the drawbridge and offers horses to Calmer.
source_quote: Thurne shouts, “I can cook something nice with those legs. Tastes like chicken.”

subject: Zinia
fact: Zinia is a masked spy who has been observing the group. He is perceptive, quick to react, and survives the frog ambush unharmed. He rescues Calmer from the water, kills a frog, and witnesses the final frog die from an arrow. He is deeply unimpressed by the party’s incompetence.
source_quote: Zinia mutters to himself that this is not the kind of start that will ingratiate him with the clerics of St. Cuthbert.

subject: Sequoia
fact: Sequoia is injured during the bridge collapse and is dragged to camp by Thorne. He is pragmatic, takes charge after Calmer’s failure, and leads the group toward the moathouse door. He observes the state of the entrance and notes signs of recent traffic.
source_quote: Sequoia decides that he can lead, but Sequoia will observe.

subject: St. Cuthbert's Clerics
fact: Clerics of St. Cuthbert are expected to lead in dangerous situations, as Calmer believes. Their traditions are rigid, and Calmer’s failure to uphold them causes him shame.
source_quote: Calmer shouts, “I think it’s time that I did what all great clerics of St. Cuthbert do, which is lead.”

subject: Giant Frogs
fact: Four giant frogs ambush the party near the drawbridge, missing Zinia. Two more jump onto the bridge during its collapse. Four frogs are killed in combat; one is killed by Zinia, one by Zephyr, one by an arrow, and one by Sequoia. Two frogs are injured by the collapse. Their presence is tied to the moathouse’s decay.
source_quote: Four giant frogs jump out of the pool near the bridge and attack.

subject: Moathouse
fact: The Moathouse is a decaying ruin surrounded by a treacherous, overgrown path. The drawbridge is rotting and collapses under weight. The courtyard has a broken door, shattered stairs, and signs of recent human and animal traffic. The surrounding land is a boggy, unhealthy marsh with thick vegetation, strange sounds, and dangerous terrain.
source_quote: The bogs stink. The vegetation appears dense and prolific, but somehow sickly and unhealthy, creepers and vines throwing their strangling loops over the skeletons of dead saplings and living bushes alike.

subject: Track to the Moathouse
fact: The path to the Moathouse is overgrown, washed out in places, and littered with fallen trees and mire. It is barely passable, requiring hours to traverse on foot or horseback. Game still uses the path, leaving faint traces. The land slopes downward into a swamp near the ruins.
source_quote: The track here is only about 15 feet wide or so, with crumbling embankments making travel near the edge dangerous.

subject: Bridge Collapse
fact: The drawbridge collapses under the weight of Calmer and Zinia’s advance, causing Calmer and Sequoia to fall into the water. Two frogs are injured by the collapse. Zinia survives, and Zephyr remains standing. The collapse triggers a second wave of frog attacks.
source_quote: The frogs' and the party's weight causes the bridge to shatter.

subject: Frog Ambush
fact: A total of six giant frogs attack the party: four near the bridge, two on the collapsing drawbridge. All are killed. Zinia kills one, Zephyr kills one, an arrow kills one, and Sequoia kills one. The ambush is poorly coordinated but deadly due to the terrain.
source_quote: The last ribbit," he thinks. A few seconds later, the ground is drenched in the blood of giant frogs.

subject: Drawbridge
fact: The drawbridge to the Moathouse is rotted and structurally unsound. It collapses under the weight of the party, killing no one directly but causing injuries and triggering a second wave of attacks. Its condition was unnoticed until too late.
source_quote: At the last moment, the masked spy notices the bridge rotting.

subject: Unexplained Traffic
fact: Zephyr observes signs of recent human and pack animal traffic leading to the Moathouse, suggesting other parties have recently passed through. The origin and purpose of this traffic are unknown.
source_quote: Zephyr shouts, “Hm, this is interesting. Some human and pack animal traffic comes this way.”

subject: Planting 16, 579
fact: The events of the chapter occur on Planting 16, 579. This is the day the party assembles, travels to the Moathouse, and engages in the frog ambush and bridge collapse.
source_quote: Date: Planting 16, 579

subject: Voss
fact: Voss is a former bandit who was coerced into service due to gambling debts, alcoholism, and the forced sale of his property; he is terrified of being executed by the Church of St. Cuthbert for alleged cult membership.
source_quote: The Moathouse was a good hideout because nobody wanted to come here anymore. The Temple was dead, and adventurers picked this place clean, so nobody came here.

subject: Calmer
fact: Calmer is a cleric of St. Cuthbert who takes grim pleasure in explaining the Church’s punitive doctrines, deliberately exacerbating Voss’s terror under the guise of 'calming' him.
source_quote: I think it’s important that we call to calm down.

subject: Sequoia
fact: Sequoia is a rogue who shows reluctant empathy toward Voss, rejecting execution in favor of interrogation, and is the first to notice and investigate the mysterious symbol.
source_quote: Look, I know you are just a desperate man caught up in something bigger than themselves. And I really don’t need to hand you over to the authorities. I just need to know what this symbol is.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr is a monk who uses illusion magic to manipulate enemies and is dismissive of Voss’s knowledge, believing him too low on the hierarchy to be useful.
source_quote: He’s too low down the totem pole to know anything useful.

subject: Zinia
fact: Zinia is a rogue who executes precise, silent takedowns and follows Sequoia’s lead in interrogation, showing no overt emotion but contributing to the group’s tactical cohesion.
source_quote: Keep him alive. We want to interrogate him.

subject: Church of St. Cuthbert
fact: The Church of St. Cuthbert enforces brutal penalties for suspected membership in rival cults, treating affiliation as a capital offense; its reputation for zealous punishment has instilled terror in the region.
source_quote: Membership in the cult is punishable by death.

subject: The Moathouse
fact: The Moathouse was once a religious site tied to a now-dead temple, later used as a bandit hideout after being thoroughly looted and abandoned by adventurers; it is now a scene of recent violence and death.
source_quote: The Moathouse was a good hideout because nobody wanted to come here anymore. The Temple was dead, and adventurers picked this place clean, so nobody came here.

subject: Flat river rock with eye and tear
fact: A small, inscribed river stone bearing the symbol of an eye and a tear; it was given by a higher authority to signify belonging to a hidden network, and its presence triggers extreme fear in Voss.
source_quote: It’s what the big boss gave the boss who gave it to us. It meant we belonged.

subject: Bandits
fact: A group of armed outlaws, formerly tied to the Moathouse’s ruined temple; most were killed in a surprise attack by the party, three escaped through an enlarged arrow slit, and one remains alive for interrogation.
source_quote: Three of the bandits escape to the south through an arrow slit that has been enlarged to allow easy retreat.

subject: Moathouse raid
fact: The party launched a coordinated, stealthy assault on the Moathouse, killing nine bandits and capturing one; the attack began with illusion-based door manipulation and ended with the group securing the site for interrogation.
source_quote: Zephyr has used an illusion to get the folks inside to open the door for us.

subject: The Eye and Tear Symbol
fact: The origin and meaning of the eye-and-tear symbol remain unknown; it is linked to a higher authority within a hidden network, possibly tied to the dead temple or a secret cult, and its presence suggests a deeper conspiracy.
source_quote: It’s what the big boss gave the boss who gave it to us. It meant we belonged.

subject: session date
fact: The events occur during a single session of play, marked by a sequence of combat, interrogation, and revelation, culminating in the discovery of the eye-and-tear symbol and the bandit’s emotional breakdown.
source_quote: Sequoia then wakes up the bandit.
